missed_subsystems: Heroku deployment manifest and process runtime — app.json (Heroku app descriptor declaring MONGODB_URI env, NODE_ENV=production, NPM_CONFIG_ONLY, and a postdeploy hook running artifacts/db-reset.js that re-seeds default accounts on every deploy) plus Procfile (web process run under the `forever` process manager). recon captures Docker/compose (C21) and CI (C22) but not this distinct PaaS deploy target / runtime, which carries its own supply-chain and data-seeding exposure. Paths: /tmp/eval_targets/nodegoat/app.json, /tmp/eval_targets/nodegoat/Procfile
notes: recon.json is broad and accurate; nearly every risk-bearing surface in the repo is enumerated. Independent inventory of /tmp/eval_targets/nodegoat: routes in app/routes/index.js register the same handlers recon lists (session/profile/contributions/benefits/allocations/memos/research/learn/tutorial/error), and the GET-vs-POST splits recon omits (GET /login, GET /signup, GET /memos) are trivial since the same handlers/views are already covered. The vulnerable specifics recon flagged check out against source: SSRF via needle.get(req.query.url+req.query.symbol) in app/routes/research.js; open redirect at GET /learn (res.redirect(req.query.url)); commented-out helmet/csurf/nosniff and HTTPS, swig autoescape:false, MemoryStore session, hardcoded cookieSecret/cryptoKey in config/env/all.js; benefits A7 function-level-access fix commented out in index.js; committed TLS key/cert and ZAP api key. Two genuine-but-modest gaps: (1) the Heroku deploy surface above; (2) app/data/research-dao.js exists but is not in recon — it is an inert stub (getBySymbol builds an unused searchCriteria and returns nothing, no DB call), so its omission hides no real risk and is treated as trivial. Other unlisted files (config.js loader, config/env/production.js={}, Gruntfile.js with grunt-retire/jshint tooling, test/security/profile-test.js Selenium+ZAP harness that reuses the committed zapApiKey) are dev/build tooling, not production attack surface. Net: the coverage denominator is trustworthy; the only non-trivial missed subsystem is the Heroku/Procfile+app.json deployment path. Counts: recon = 22 components + 7 data_stores + 15 entry_points + 6 trust_boundaries + 9 external_deps = 59; independent ~= 62 (adds Heroku deploy surface, research-dao stub, and the GET form pages collapsed into existing handlers).
